declarations.description:
A checkbox: a yes or no choice that is saved with a form, or a way to pick
items from a list. Use a switch for a setting that applies at once, and
radios when exactly one of several choices must be picked.

- A native `<input type="checkbox">` in shadow DOM, drawn over with a box
  and mark. Space, label clicks and the tab order are the browser's, and
  indeterminate shows as `mixed` with no script.
- Named by `label` (and any default-slot content) through a real `<label>`.
  The label is visible by default; `hide-label` hides it from sight only.
  Put help text in the `description` slot and the message for a failed check
  in the `error` slot.
- Joins the surrounding form: submits `value` (default "on") under `name`
  while checked, and nothing otherwise. `required` makes an unchecked box
  fail validation. Resets to its starting state with the form. The native
  input lives in shadow DOM, so the host mirrors its value and validity
  through ElementInternals.
- `indeterminate` is for a parent of a partly picked group. The next user
  click clears it and toggles the box, as a native checkbox does.
- Fires `input` and `change` after each user toggle.
- Motion: pressing squishes the box; letting go springs it back with a
  small pop. Checking grows the fill out of the centre, then draws the
  check in with a tiny overshoot, in about 450ms; unchecking runs it back.
  The indeterminate dash and the check turn into each other. A tap during a
  move turns it round from where it is, with its speed. A soft pass of
  light crosses the fill as it grows. Transform and opacity move, and the
  check's stroke offset draws it in (paint only, no layout). Nothing
  animates on first paint; a change from code moves the same way as a
  click. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the state changes at once
  and the colour fades over 120ms.
- State is never colour alone: the check or dash is drawn on the fill.
- The hover, selected and pressed fills come from the shared state layer.
declarations.name: PrismCheckbox

A grid or single-column list of cards, with paging, selection that is kept
across pages, and the loading, empty and error states. NAME PROVISIONAL. Section owns these states on a real page; this element
gives them a default look and fires events so a Section can take over.

```html
<prism-card-list label="Resources" selection="multi" total="120" page="2">
  <prism-card type="selectable" kind="collection" value="h-13">…</prism-card>
</prism-card-list>
```

- **Layout.** Columns follow the list's own width (a container query), not
  the screen: under 640px one column, 640 to 1023 two, 1024 to 1279 three,
  1280 and up four. Cards stay at least 280px wide, the gap is space-4 (16px)
  and cards in a row share a height. `columns="1"` pins one column (Aside,
  Drawer, Modal). No masonry.
- **Semantics.** An inner wrapper around the cards is the labelled `list` and
  each card a `listitem` (the card sets its own role). The host has no role,
  so the selected count, pager and status region sit outside the list. Titles stay real headings: give every card
  the same `level`, one below the Section heading. With `total` set, each
  card gets `aria-posinset` and `aria-setsize` from the data, not from what
  is on the page.
- **Paging.** Server-side: you swap the children when `prism-card-list-page`
  fires. `page-size` is 12, 24 or 48 (default 24). The pager shows even when
  there is one page. A `pagination` slot replaces it with a real Pagination
  component; `load-more` shows a "Load more" button instead.
- **Selection** uses the same cards, `value` ids and controller as
  `prism-card-group`, multi only (use a group for a single choice). Ids not
  on screen stay selected when the page changes; a visible "N selected" and
  "Clear selection" sit above the cards unless `hide-selection-bar` is set
  or you fill the `toolbar` slot.
- **States** (`state`): `loading` (skeleton cards, list busy, polite
  "Loading"), `refreshing` (cards stay, quiet busy line), `empty` (fill the
  `empty` slot), `no-matches` ("No matches" and Clear filters), `error`
  (what failed and Retry). A single failed card uses `state="error"` on the
  card itself.

A bar that shows how far something has got. Common props: `value`, `max`,

- A native `<progress>` named by a real `<label for>`. Leave `value` off

  under 24px hides its tail (`:state(tiny)`), a full bar drops the glow

declarations.description:
A group of radios where exactly one can be picked, and the value of the
pick is what the form submits.

- A native `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>` carrying `label`. Put help text in
  the `description` slot and the message for a failed check in the `error`
  slot.
- Each child `prism-radio` is drawn as a native `<input type="radio">` with
  a real `<label>`, all in this one shadow root so they share a name. Tab
  stop, arrow keys and Space are the browser's, with no key handling here.
  Chrome and Firefox wrap round at the ends and flip Left and Right in
  right-to-left text; WebKit does neither, as for any native radios.
  A radio's `slot` attribute is used by the group while it is a child, and
  put back when it leaves.
- `value` is the picked radio's `value` (empty: none). It is what is
  submitted under `name`; the inputs are in shadow DOM, so the group mirrors
  the value and validity through ElementInternals. `required` fails
  validation while none is picked. A radio with `checked` in the markup sets
  the starting value. Resets to the starting value with the form.
- Fires `input` and `change` after each user pick.
- Disabling the group disables every radio in it.
- Motion: pressing squishes the dot's box; the dot springs in with a
  gentle overshoot as the ring turns to the accent, about 400ms. The radio

declarations.description:
Shows that something is running right now: a solid dot that breathes, with
one ring that spreads out of it and fades, like light leaving a prism. Use it
beside a task or card title while a job is in progress, and remove it (or
swap it for a Tag that says "Done") when the job ends.

  always in the page for screen readers; `show-label` also shows it.

  box that scales with the size.

  success, warning or danger. Use success for "online".

  60% to nothing while the dot swells from 4 to 4.6 and back, both in step.
  One pulse takes 1.92s, then it rests for 800ms before the next (a 2.72s
  cycle). In the rest the ring is gone and the dot is still. Under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` it holds still as the dot with a faint
  ring. The dot is always there, so motion is never the only signal.
- It does not show progress. For a known amount of work use Progress.

declarations.description:
A row of mutually exclusive choices that share one sliding indicator, like a
set of radio buttons drawn as a switch between views: `<prism-segmented-control
label="Range"><prism-segment value="day">Day</prism-segment>…`.

- A native `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>` carrying `label` (`hide-label`
  keeps it for screen readers only). Put help text in the `description` slot
  and the message for a failed check in the `error` slot.
- Each child `prism-segment` is drawn as a native `<input type="radio">` inside
  a real `<label>`, all in this one shadow root so they share a name. Tab
  stop, arrow keys (all four, skipping disabled segments) and Space are the
  browser's, with no key handling here. Chrome and Firefox also wrap round at
  the ends and flip Left and Right in right-to-left text; WebKit does
  neither, as for any native radios.
- `value` is the picked segment's `value` (empty: none, and no indicator).
  It is what is submitted under `name`. `required` fails validation while
  none is picked. A segment with `checked` in the markup sets the starting
  value. Resets to the starting value with the form.
- Fires `input` and `change` after each user pick.
- Disabling the control disables every segment in it.
- With polish motion on, pressing scales the segment evenly (about 3%) and
  it eases back. Otherwise, and under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, only
  the press colour shows.
- Each segment's parts also carry `checked` and `disabled` while they apply,
  so a theme can target `::part(segment checked)`.
- Sizes `sm`, `md`, `lg` follow the control heights and density. `full-width`
  shares the row equally.
- With polish motion on, the indicator slides to the picked segment on two
  springs (one per edge) so it stretches on the way, about 325ms
  (`--prism-motion-segmented`), with a small overshoot that never leaves the
  track. A new pick during the move turns it round from where it is.
  Transform and opacity only. Nothing moves on first paint, on a resize, or
  when the width of a segment changes: the indicator just follows. A change
  from code moves the same way as a click. Without polish motion, and under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the indicator jumps to a static selected
  surface and the colours change at once.

Four behaviors, split by what a person can do (not by colour):
- read-only (default): a label, no click.
- `dismissible`: a remove button ("Remove {text}"); fires `prism-tag-remove`.
  The tag does not remove itself: the app decides.
- `selectable`: a toggle button (`aria-pressed`); fires `prism-tag-select`.
- `trigger`: a button that opens something (a Select) and shows a caret in
  the trailing slot; fires `prism-tag-trigger`. It looks like any other Tag.

A Tag never navigates. For a link use a link. For a count or Live / Running
/ Stopped use Badge.

Accessibility: the text is the name and the meaning, so colour is never the
only signal. Put a short word in the tag (a few words, no wrapping). An
icon only helps reading. Interactive tags are at least 24px high even at
`size="sm"` (WCAG 2.5.8).

while there is a value. `prefix` and `suffix` slots hold short decorative
text or an icon (a currency sign, a unit); put anything the user needs in
the label or description, since an affix is not part of the input's name.
